commands.review_summary:
The PR updates reply normalization to strip a leading `NO_REPLY` token when whitespace separates it from subsequent word content and adds regression tests for that behavior.

PR surface: Source +22, Tests +30. Total +52 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main does not recognize a leading `NO_REPLY` followed by whitespace and substantive content, so the provided payload reaches delivery unchanged. A live current-main channel reproduction was not run.

target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103735. Follow-up to #30916 and #30955.

When a model emits `NO_REPLY` on its own line before the real reply body:

```
NO_REPLY

Wait — the user mentioned me directly. I should respond.

Hi! How can I help?
```

…the literal `NO_REPLY` token and any interstitial reasoning text are **delivered to the channel** alongside the real reply. The sentinel should be stripped (or the entire reply suppressed if nothing substantive remains).

## Root Cause

`startsWithSilentToken` (`tokens.ts:280`) uses `getSilentLeadingAttachedRegex` which requires the token to be **glued** to a letter or number via `(?=[\p{L}\p{N}])`. A newline/whitespace-separated leading token — the most common preamble shape — is not detected as a leading sentinel, so `stripLeadingSilentToken` is never called. The `stripSilentToken` fallback only handles **trailing** tokens (`\s*$`), so the leading token survives the mixed-content branch entirely.

The punctuation safe harbour (`NO_REPLY: explanation` and `NO_REPLY -- nope`) is preserved because punctuation after a token is not a sentinel — it is natural language.

## Fix

In the mixed-content branch of `normalizeReplyPayload`, add a targeted check: when the glued-attached detection fails, test whether the leading token is separated from real content by **whitespace followed by a word character** (`\s+[\p{L}\p{N}]`). This catches `NO_REPLY\n\nWait...` and `NO_REPLY  The answer...` without affecting the punctuation safe harbour.

```typescript
// After glued-attached check fails:
else if (text.length > silentToken.length) {
  const trimmed = text.trimStart();
  const afterToken = trimmed.slice(silentToken.length);
  if (
    trimmed.toLowerCase().startsWith(silentToken.toLowerCase()) &&
    /^\s+[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(afterToken)
  ) {
    text = stripLeadingSilentToken(text, silentToken);
  }
}
```

## Behavioral Proof

Run `node proof-103735-sentinel.cjs`:

```
Test                       | Old (leaks)                           | New (fixed)
Newline-separated          | "NO_REPLY\n\nWait -- user..."          | "Wait -- user..."           <- FIXED
Space-separated            | "NO_REPLY  The answer is 42."          | "The answer is 42."         <- FIXED
Tab-separated              | "NO_REPLY\tThe answer is 42."          | "The answer is 42."         <- FIXED
Nl + trailing              | "NO_REPLY\n\nHello"                    | "Hello"                     <- FIXED
Glued leading              | "The user is saying hello"             | "The user is saying hello"  (unchanged)
Colon after (keep)         | "NO_REPLY: explanation"                | "NO_REPLY: explanation"     (unchanged)
Dash after (keep)          | "NO_REPLY—note"                        | "NO_REPLY—note"             (unchanged)
Sp+punctuation (keep)      | "NO_REPLY -- nope"                     | "NO_REPLY -- nope"          (unchanged)
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.ts` | 12 lines added in mixed-content branch |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` | 3 new regression tests |

## New Regression Tests

| Test | Input | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY | `"NO_REPLY\n\nWait — …\n\nHi!"` | `"Wait — …\n\nHi!"` (no token) |
| strips leading NO_REPLY separated by spaces | `"NO_REPLY  The answer is 42."` | `"The answer is 42."` (no token) |
| suppresses when stripping leaves only whitespace | `"NO_REPLY\n\n\n  "` | `null` (silent skip) |

Existing tests continue to pass — the punctuation safe harbour (`": explanation"`, `"—note"`, `" -- nope"`) is preserved.

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency. Related: #97638 ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled: 1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace. 2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts. 3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. Prompt respects configured `skills.limits.maxSkillsInPrompt` and `maxSkillsPromptChars`. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides. 4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution. ## User Impact ```json5 { agents: { defaults: { sandbox: { skipSkillsSync: true, docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" } } } } } ``` Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`. ## Evidence ### Real behavior proof (Docker container) *Screenshot: terminal output from container (commit ) showing skipSkillsSync in Docker backend, preinstalled skill at , sandbox-readable paths in prompt, and 12/12 tests passing.* *Screenshot: terminal output from container with commit `94b0d8ecf18`.* ``` ====================================================== Real Behavior Proof: skipSkillsSync Feature Container: openclaw-sandbox-test:latest Commit: 94b0d8ecf18 ====================================================== >>> 1. Config: skipSkillsSync=true { "agents": { "defaults": { "sandbox": { "mode": "all", "skipSkillsSync": true } } } } >>> 2. Sandbox explain: mode=all, sandboxed=true mode: all sandboxed: True >>> 3. Unit tests: 12 passed Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 12 passed (9) >>> 4. Code behavior: all OK SandboxConfig type : OK Config resolver : OK computeSkillsEligibility : OK Context branching : OK Name-only prompt (no paths) : OK XML escaping : OK Command prompt guard : OK Workspace info propagation : OK CLI runner propagation : OK Config labels : OK FIELD_HELP : OK Config baseline : OK Docs : OK ====================================================== ALL VERIFICATIONS PASSED ====================================================== ``` ### Test coverage (12 tests pass, 0 failures) - drops host snapshot and builds name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled - drops host snapshot (no remapping) when `skipSkillsSync` is absent (regression guard) - keeps snapshots for non-sandboxed runs (regression guard) - eligibility preserved in sandbox prompts (regression guard) - rebuilds sandbox prompts from materialized skill paths - preserves remote eligibility when rebuilding sandbox prompts - falls back to effective workspace for older sandbox contexts - escapes XML-special characters in skill names when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled - maps materialized read paths while preserving original file identities - respects char limit with many skills fitting within 18000 chars - truncates when total exceeds MAX_SKILLS_PROMPT_CHARS - preserves remote eligibility note in skip-mode name-only prompt ### Changed files (14 files) | File | Change | |------|--------| | `src/config/types.agents-shared.ts` | Type definition for `skipSkillsSync` | | `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Zod schema with safe-use contract | | `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Config UI labels | | `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Config help text | | `src/agents/sandbox/types.ts` | `SandboxConfig.skipSkillsSync` + `SandboxWorkspaceInfo.skipSkillsSync` | | `src/agents/sandbox/config.ts` | Config resolver propagation | | `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts` | Extracted `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` helper + branching + stale cleanup | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.ts` | Name-only prompt + XML escaping + configured prompt limits | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.test.ts` | 6 new test cases (11 total) | | `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | Pass `skipSkillsSync` + `config` to sandbox context | | `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-system-prompt.ts` | Early return guard against host snapshot fallthrough | | `src/skills/loading/workspace.ts` | Export `resolveSkillsLimits` and `prepareSyncedSkillsDirectory` | | `docs/gateway/sandboxing.md` | Document `skipSkillsSync` in Skills Note | | `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated baseline |
